facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence and limitations
facts.text: - Perimeter and comparability. The 10-K says the FY2025 statements include the merged business for the full year while FY2024 does not (page:118). Evidence: the statement of FY2024 perimeter. Risk mechanism: year-on-year growth for FY2025 over FY2024 is not like for like. Consequence: CP-1 must label that comparison and prefer the quarterly comparatives, which are both post-merger. - Revenue base changes. The Q3 10-Q attributes lower revenue to contracts moving from consolidated to unconsolidated joint ventures and to fiscal year 2025 divestitures (page:23, page:25). Evidence: MD&A text. Risk mechanism: reported revenue and equity earnings are not comparable across periods. Consequence: the model should carry equity earnings and distributions separately. - Management measures. Net leverage and Adjusted EBITDA are defined by management in the release (page:10). A figure computed by an analyst from statement lines will differ in definition. Consequence: both must be shown and labelled. - Off-balance-sheet and contingent claims. Sales of receivables under the MARPA are disclosed (Q3 10-Q page:9); the debt note excludes them. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 should not read the debt table as the full financing claim without that note.

Adjusted EBITDA and net leverage appear only as management measures with a reconciliation.

The executed credit agreement and the first amendment of April 24, 2026 are not in the pack; the Q3 10-Q lists the amendment as Exhibit 10.1 incorporated by reference to a Form 8-K filed April 28, 2026

Post-amendment financial maintenance covenant level is not stated in the Q3 10-Q, which says only that a financial covenant applies in certain circumstances to the Term Loan A and Revolver and that the company was in compliance as of July 3, 2026; the maximum first lien net leverage ratio is printed only in the annual report for the pre-amendment revolver
Senior notes indenture is not supplied; coupon, maturity and guarantee terms come from the filing notes
No fourth-quarter FY2025 earnings release and no quarterly presentation slides are in the pack; the releases substitute for decks, and a text rendering cannot evidence images or charts

No credit ratings, market prices, peer or valuation data are supplied (context blank). The Q1 2026 release headline (page:1) states that Moody's upgraded the rating to Ba3 from Ba1; on the Moody's scale Ba3 sits below Ba1, so the headline is internally inconsistent, it is management narrative only, and no rating agency report is supplied to resolve it
Context names current period q2-2026 while the latest filed quarter is Q3 2026
Cash-paid interest and cash-paid taxes are not printed in any supplied source
Ownership and sponsor information is blank in the context; listed-equity shareholder detail in the annual report was not reviewed in this step
Extraction fidelity of tables was not reviewed against the original HTML filings

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Three points qualify the picture. First, cash conversion is lower than margins suggest: nine-month operating cash flow of 235 was down on 273, free cash flow of 213 includes a net 120 inflow from selling receivables, and the group is guiding to an implied fourth-quarter free cash flow of 312 to 362 to reach its 525 to 575 range. Second, the earnings base includes equity earnings of 88 on a trailing basis (7.8% of trailing Adjusted EBITDA) and management add-backs of 76 in the nine months (Adjusted EBITDA 828 against company-defined EBITDA 752), so the headline measure is more generous than a plain operating measure; the financial maintenance covenant definition is not supplied. Third, the capital structure is mostly floating and secured: 2,866 of the 3,875 is term loan debt, hedged only by swaps with notional 1.3 billion that mature through January 31, 2027, and the senior notes (1,000 at 7.250%, due August 1, 2032) sit behind the secured facilities. Tangible equity is negative (equity of 4,789 against goodwill and intangibles of 7,378), so creditor protection rests on cash flows rather than hard assets. Revenue is shrinking (nine months 2026 down 2.5%) though margins and backlog (48.2 billion) are rising. Comparability limits: FY2025 had 53 weeks, and the FY2024 base excludes the merged business until September 27, 2024, so FY2024 ratios are not shown.

facts.label: Liquidity, covenants and compliance
facts.text: Covenants. Maintenance test: a financial maintenance covenant applies "under certain circumstances"; the Q3 10-Q says it applies to the term loan A and the revolver, and that the company was in compliance as of July 3, 2026 (page:13). The level is not printed in the Q3 10-Q. The only printed level is in the 10-K for the pre-amendment facility: a maximum first lien net leverage ratio of 5.25 to 1.00 stepping down to 5.00 to 1.00 from the fifth full fiscal quarter after September 27, 2024, applying to the revolver "in certain circumstances tied to the usage of the Revolver"; the 10-K says the term loan then had no financial maintenance covenant and that a covenant breach defaults the term loan only if revolver lenders accelerate (10-K page:148). The Q3 text names term loan A as carrying the covenant, which differs from the 10-K's statement about the old term loan; the amended level and trigger are Not supplied (the amendment is not in the pack). Indicative headroom against the 10-K's 5.00x level is in Calculations; the credit agreement definition of EBITDA and of first lien net debt is not supplied and will differ. Other covenants: customary negative covenants limiting debt, liens, restricted payments, investments, asset sales and affiliate transactions in the credit agreement and indenture (10-K page:148 to page:149). The excess cash flow prepayment requirement begins with fiscal year 2026, and none had been required as of the 10-K (10-K page:147).

facts.label: Earnings quality and cash flow
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income attributable to common shareholders adjusted for interest expense and other, net, income taxes, depreciation and amortization and discrete items: acquisition, transaction and integration costs, non-cash gains and losses, loss on extinguishment of debt, utilization of fair market value adjustments from purchase accounting, and stock-based compensation (10-K page:156; Q3 release page:9). Add-backs between company-defined EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA were 110 in FY2025 (85 of acquisition and integration costs, 12 of debt extinguishment, 21 of stock compensation, less 8 of fair market value utilization), 71 in 9M 2025 and 76 in 9M 2026 (36 of integration costs, 16 of debt extinguishment, 1 of fair market value utilization, 23 of stock compensation). Equity earnings of non-consolidated subsidiaries (73 in 9M 2026) are inside both EBITDA measures; distributions received were 87 in 9M 2026 against 57 in 9M 2025, so the cash returned exceeded the earnings recognized in the latest period.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. LTM revenues to July 3, 2026 = 14,393 (FY2025) + 10,205 (9M 2026) - 10,468 (9M 2025) = 14,130. LTM operating income = 480 + 461 - 345 = 596. LTM equity earnings = 62 + 73 - 47 = 88. LTM depreciation = 40 + 25 - 29 = 36. LTM amortization = 479 + 282 - 358 = 403. LTM net income to common = 66 + 164 - 26 = 204. LTM interest expense and other, net = 353 + 209 - 261 = 301. 2. Adjusted EBITDA: FY2025 1,104. LTM to July 3, 2026 = 1,104 + 828 - 804 = 1,128, equal to the 1,128 printed (Q3 release page:10). 9M 2026 = 263 + 275 + 290 = 828 (quarterly releases page:1) and = 324 + 504 = 828 by segment (Q3 10-Q page:26 to page:27). 9M 2025 = 321 + 483 = 804. Q2 LTM = 1,104 + (263 + 275) - (262 + 268) = 1,112, equal to the printed 1,112 (Q2 release page:11). 3. facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Amentum is a global advanced engineering and technology solutions provider to U.S. and allied governments, organised in two segments (Digital Solutions and Global Engineering Solutions). It exists in its present form since September 27, 2024, when the Jacobs Critical Mission Solutions business and parts of the Jacobs Divergent Solutions business were spun off and merged with the legacy Amentum business in a Reverse Morris Trust. Creditors therefore lend to a company that has existed as a combined entity for about two years, that carries purchase-accounting intangibles and goodwill (7,378 of 11,199 of total assets at July 3, 2026), and whose pre-merger history does not include the larger business.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The operating model is low-capital and contract-based. Roughly four-fifths of revenue is from the U.S. Government, mostly as prime contractor, with about 56% of 9M 2026 revenue on cost-plus-fee contracts that pass through inflation and a rising fixed-price share. Visibility is large in headline terms (backlog 48.2 billion) but only 6.2 billion is funded, so revenue durability depends on appropriations and option exercise rather than signed funding. The principal operating risks the filings describe are budget timing (shutdowns from October 2, 2025 to November 12, 2025 and a partial shutdown from January 31, 2026 to February 3, 2026), contract compliance and audit exposure, joint venture structure changes that reduce consolidated revenue while moving profit into equity earnings, and estimate catch-ups on fixed-price work.

The weaknesses for a creditor are in control and documentation rather than behaviour: the sponsor-linked stockholder keeps board nomination rights tied to its ownership, the tax-free merger structure restricts some strategic actions, and the credit agreement, its April 2026 amendment, the indenture and the tax matters agreement are not supplied, so capacity to pay out cash, incur debt or release collateral cannot be tested. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The defining transaction closed on September 27, 2024. Legacy Amentum (Amentum Parent Holdings LLC, owned by Amentum Joint Venture LP) merged with the spin-off of the Jacobs Critical Mission Solutions business and portions of the Jacobs Divergent Solutions business in a tax-efficient Reverse Morris Trust. Amentum Parent Holdings LLC was the accounting acquirer and is the predecessor, so statements before September 27, 2024 exclude the acquired business and are not comparable (10-K page:117, page:128). Before the spin-off the acquired business reorganised under a new company, distributed a cash payment of about 911 million to Jacobs, and Jacobs distributed about 80.95% of its shares to Jacobs shareholders (10-K page:6 to page:7, page:128). Immediately after closing there were about 243 million shares outstanding, held 58.5% by Jacobs and its shareholders and 37.0% by Amentum Joint Venture LP, with 4.5% placed in escrow; in March 2025 the escrow was released, 3.5% to the former Jacobs holders and 1.0% to the sponsor stockholder (10-K page:128). Consideration transferred was 3,948 and total consideration 4,032 including a previously held joint venture interest, and goodwill was recognised at 3,004 on final allocation (10-K page:129 to page:131). Status: completed, with purchase accounting finalised in FY2025.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Later debt events. In FY2025 the company made voluntary term loan payments of about 191 (June 27, 2025), 250 (July 31, 2025) and 281 (September 30, 2025), together 722, after selling the Rapid Solutions hardware and product business, part of Digital Solutions, to Lockheed Martin Corporation on June 26, 2025 for 360 in cash (10-K page:98, page:105, page:132, page:145). On April 24, 2026 a first amendment to the credit facility (executed; the amendment itself is not in the pack) created a 1,400 term loan A due April 24, 2031, amended the existing term loan into a 1,591 term loan B due September 27, 2031 on lower margins, and raised the revolver by 150 to 1,000 with maturity April 24, 2031 (Q2 10-Q page:17; Q3 10-Q page:11 to page:12). The Q2 2026 release headline describes the term loan A proceeds as used to repay and reprice term loan B (management language, Q2 release page:1). A further voluntary 125 payment on term loan B was made on June 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:12). Subsequent to the quarter end, only the August 10, 2026 earnings release (updated FY2026 guidance, with revenue lowered and Adjusted EBITDA low end raised) and the August 11, 2026 filing are in the pack; no later debt transaction is evidenced up to the cutoff. Sponsor: the filing refers to the equityholder and its affiliates as private equity firms (10-K page:70) but the context names no sponsor and the consulting agreement partners American Securities LLC and Lindsay Goldberg LLC are named only as former advisers (10-K page:153); this handoff does not infer more.

facts.label: Capital allocation, acquisitions and disclosure
facts.text: Capital allocation has prioritised debt: cash from the Rapid Solutions sale and operations funded 722 of voluntary term loan payments in FY2025, and a further 125 was paid in FY2026, with no dividend or buyback (see above). The leverage effect is in the financial handoff (net leverage 3.23x at October 3, 2025 and 3.03x at July 3, 2026). The business strategy states reliance in part on acquisitions and strategic investments to sustain growth, as well as targeted divestitures (10-K page:23 risk factor list); one acquisition-related cash outflow (70, the working capital settlement for the Transaction) and one divestiture occurred in FY2025 (10-K page:116, page:130), and 9M 2026 shows no acquisition spend (Q3 10-Q page:4). No acquisition appetite is inferred from these. Contributions to equity method investments were 53 in 9M 2026 against 36 in 9M 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:4), a use of cash that supports the joint venture strategy. Disclosure quality is high for the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, net leverage and segment data, but monitoring lacks: the current debt schedule (no maturity table at July 3, 2026), the credit agreement covenant certificate and definitions, and an add-back bridge to the covenant definition.

No acquisition appetite is inferred from these. Contributions to equity method investments were 53 in 9M 2026 against 36 in 9M 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:4), a use of cash that supports the joint venture strategy. Disclosure quality is high for the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, net leverage and segment data, but monitoring lacks: the current debt schedule (no maturity table at July 3, 2026), the credit agreement covenant certificate and definitions, and an add-back bridge to the covenant definition.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: 81% of revenue from direct U.S. Government contracts, backlog of 48.2 billion with 6.2 billion funded (10-K page:8; Q3 10-Q page:27). Risk mechanic: customer credit risk is minimal, but appropriations delays, continuing resolutions and shutdowns defer awards, billing and cash collection; unfunded backlog converts only as funding arrives. Credit implication: debt service risk comes from timing and liquidity, not demand collapse; a liquidity cushion of 1,376 at July 3, 2026 (financial handoff) is the relevant mitigant. Counter: the rating-statement conflict does not affect this. 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: fixed-price share rose to 29% of 9M 2026 revenue from 24% in FY2025, and net favorable estimate adjustments of 83 against 40 (Q3 10-Q page:8, page:27). Risk mechanic: fixed-price work carries cost overrun risk and catch-up adjustments move reported profit between periods. Credit implication: Adjusted EBITDA of 1,128 on a trailing basis may include non-recurring catch-up benefit; leverage of 3.44x gross and 3.03x net is more sensitive to margin slippage than the headline suggests. Counter: cost-plus work remains 56% of revenue. 3. Concentration. Evidence: Department of War and Intelligence Community 5,334 of 10,205 in 9M 2026, and the U.S. Government at 80% in total (Q3 10-Q page:7). Risk mechanic: shifts in defense or intelligence budgets, contract recompetes, or protests concentrate effects. Credit implication: single-sovereign dependence limits diversification; debarment or a large program loss is a tail risk with the greatest effect on enterprise value and on a collateral package secured by substantially all assets. 4. Sponsor alignment and creditor control. Evidence: no dividends and repurchases, voluntary prepayments, board nomination rights linked to ownership, tax-free merger restrictions (10-K page:24, page:71, page:93). Risk mechanic: a holder with board influence could favour distributions or recapitalisations when leverage falls; the restricted-payment capacity in the credit agreement is not visible. Credit implication: current behaviour supports deleveraging, but the sources do not allow a view on whether the documents would stop a distribution; monitoring should track holder changes and the amended credit agreement. 5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: no credit agreement, amendment, indenture or tax matters agreement in the pack; no ratings report; current holdings unknown. Risk mechanic: covenant, priming and payout analysis cannot be performed. Credit implication: conclusions on creditor control are provisional.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Amentum Holdings, Inc. has an adequate and improving credit profile with sound liquidity, but its leverage, thin cash conversion and untested loan documents leave limited room for error. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,376 million, net leverage of 3.03x (3.23x at FY2025) and cash interest cover of 3.93x, backed by revenue that is 81% U.S. Government and a backlog of USD 48.2 billion. The weakest point is cash generation: nine-month free cash flow of USD 213 million falls to USD 93 million without a USD 120 million receivable-sales inflow, and guidance implies fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 312 million to USD 362 million. The outcome turns on whether that cash arrives, on the expiry of USD 1.3 billion of interest rate swaps by January 31, 2027, and on credit agreement terms the sources do not supply.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, liquidity and refinancing risk are low in the near term. The group holds cash of USD 459 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 917 million, a total of USD 1,376 million (Documentary Fact; financial handoff liquidity table). facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Liquidity (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): USD 1,376 million of liquidity with no drawings on the revolver and the first committed maturity in April 2031. Deleveraging record (Documentary Fact; financial and business handoffs): total debt fell from USD 4,008 million to USD 3,875 million, net leverage from 3.23x to 3.03x, with voluntary term loan payments of USD 722 million in FY2025 and USD 125 million in June 2026 and no dividends or buybacks. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Cash conversion (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; financial handoff): free cash flow of USD 93 million in the nine months excluding receivable sales, against a reported USD 213 million; the programme has a maximum of USD 400 million and USD 300 million was sold and outstanding. Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation; both handoffs): Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,128 million against USD 1,013 million before adjustments; equity earnings inside the measure; a 53-week trailing period; and a rise of USD 43 million in net favorable estimate adjustments that exceeds the USD 24 million rise in nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, which suggests underlying earnings growth was smaller, although the filing does not give the EBITDA effect. Interest-rate exposure (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): about 74% of debt is floating rate, hedged by swaps of USD 1.3 billion that mature through January 31, 2027, and the company puts the nine-month sensitivity at about USD 23 million per one percentage point. Balance sheet composition (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): goodwill and intangibles of USD 7,378 million are 66% of total assets, so tangible equity is negative USD 2,589 million, and creditor value rests on contract cash flows. Revenue and funding conditionality (Documentary Fact; business handoff): funded backlog is 12.9% of total backlog, revenue declined 2.5% in the nine months, and fixed-price work rose to 29% of revenue from 24%. Documentation and control (Insufficient Information; business handoff): no loan documents, ratings or current ownership, so payout capacity, collateral release and covenant headroom cannot be tested; the tax-free merger structure also limits some strategic actions.

spans.text: ## Request

Entity: Amentum Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: AMTM; Delaware registrant, Commission File Number 001-42176; cover of the quarterly report for the period ended July 3, 2026, page:1). As-of date: 2026-11-05. Evidence cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency: USD, stated in millions in the statements.

Question for this step: can the supplied source set support the requested downstream work (CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5, the minimum module set), and what remains blocked? This step gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it does not normalise, reconcile or recalculate any figure.

Period labelling used throughout. Amentum's fiscal year ends on the Friday nearest September 30. FY2025 is the 53-week year ended October 3, 2025, with the 53rd week in the fourth quarter (10-K page:118). FY2024 ended September 27, 2024 (52 weeks). Fiscal Q1 2026 ended January 2, 2026, Q2 ended April 3, 2026, Q3 ended July 3, 2026.

Context mismatch to carry forward. The run context names the current period as `q2-2026` and the prior period as `fy-2025`. The latest filed quarter in the pack is fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended July 3, 2026; 10-Q signed August 11, 2026, page:32; earnings release dated August 10, 2026), which falls before the cutoff. The Q2 2026 filings are also in the pack. This step treats Q3 2026 (three months and nine months) as the latest balance-sheet and liquidity date, keeps Q2 2026 available as the labelled context period, and leaves the choice of headline period to the downstream modules, which must state it. No currency mismatch: sources report USD.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

### Readiness view

The effective source set is sufficient for the requested snapshot work, with bounded limitations; it is not complete for a covenant, legal or market-based read. Filed financial statements and notes (the annual report and three quarterly reports) are the controlling authority for reported figures. The three earnings releases are management documents that supply attributed non-GAAP measures, guidance and a net leverage figure, and they do not override the filings. Readiness is a source-sufficiency view only; it is not a finding that downstream analysis is complete, and CP-MODEL input acceptance is not evaluated (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED).
| Consumer | Source readiness | Reason and bounded gaps |

| CP-1 (canonical financial data) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Statements, debt note, liquidity, segment tables and non-GAAP reconciliation are located. Limits: comparability (53-week FY2025; FY2024 excludes the merged business before September 27, 2024); the pack has no fourth-quarter FY2025 earnings release; contractual debt terms are from filing notes only. |

| CP-1A (business and transaction context) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description, the September 27, 2024 merger and spin-off description, segments, customers, backlog and contract mix are in the annual report and quarterly reports. Limits: ownership or sponsor information is not in the context; transaction documents are not supplied. |

| CP-2 (credit synthesis) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Depends on upstream handoffs, which the dependency planner sequences; that is not a source condition. Source limits are those of the two rows above plus no ratings or market evidence. |

| CP-5 (evidence trace) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Text extraction supports quote and locator checks. Limit: extraction fidelity of tables was not reviewed against the original filings, and the source text is a text rendering, so any chart or image content in the releases is not inspected. |
### Source-by-source assessment

1. Annual report, FY2025 (10-K). Document family: Form 10-K, audited. Perimeter: Amentum Holdings, Inc. and subsidiaries (page:118). Entity relationships: Amentum Parent Holdings LLC is the accounting acquirer of CMS (the Jacobs Critical Mission Solutions business and portions of Jacobs Divergent Solutions) and is the predecessor, per Note 1 (page:117 to page:118). The FY2025 statements include the merged business for the full year; the FY2024 and FY2023 statements do not include it because the transaction closed on September 27, 2024 (page:118). Debt: Note 12 table at page:144, credit facility description at page:145 to page:148, available borrowing capacity at page:147, covenant text at page:148. Liquidity discussion at page:104. Leases, Note 14 at page:151; retirement plans, Note 10 at page:139; segment note, Note 18 at page:156. Item 1A risk factors begin at page:21.

2. Quarterly report, Q1 2026 (10-Q, quarter ended January 2, 2026). Unaudited. Covenant wording at page:10; liquidity at page:21. Its debt is the original term loan structure, prior to the April 2026 amendment.

3. Quarterly report, Q2 2026 (10-Q, quarter ended April 3, 2026). Unaudited. Note 14, Subsequent Events, at page:17 records the April 24, 2026 first amendment to the credit facility, which post-dates the balance-sheet date; liquidity and covenant wording at page:26 and page:27.

4. Quarterly report, Q3 2026 (10-Q, quarter ended July 3, 2026). Unaudited. Balance sheet at page:2, statements of operations at page:2 and page:3, revenue disaggregation at page:7 and page:8, receivables sales (MARPA) at page:9, debt table at page:10, credit facility and amendment at page:11 and page:12, covenant compliance statement at page:13, segment results at page:26 and page:27, backlog at page:27 and page:28, liquidity at page:28 and page:29, risk factor statement (no material changes from the annual report) and exhibit list at page:31. The quarterly report contains no subsequent events note.

5. Earnings releases (Q1, Q2, Q3 2026). Management documents. They give reported and non-GAAP figures with a reconciliation to GAAP, fiscal-year 2026 guidance, and, in the Q3 release at page:10, a net leverage computation. The Q3 release updates guidance (page:4) and the Q1 and Q2 releases reaffirm it. Management claims are treated as attributed, supporting claims.

6. Version relationships. The three quarterly reports and three releases cover different periods and are separate active sources; none supersedes another. The Q3 10-Q is the controlling source for the latest balance sheet, and the Q2 10-Q Note 14 and the Q3 10-Q debt note both describe the same amendment. There are no duplicate files and no draft or unsigned documents.
### Coverage of the evidence needed by the objective

- Discrete quarters and fiscal years: Q3 2026 and nine months 2026 against the June 27, 2025 comparatives are in the Q3 10-Q (page:2 to page:3); Q1 and Q2 2026 are in their own reports; FY2025 is in the annual report. The 10-Q covers three and nine months; quarter versus year-to-date must be labelled by the consumer.
- Segments: two reportable segments, Digital Solutions and Global Engineering Solutions, with revenue and Adjusted EBITDA (Q3 10-Q page:26 to page:27; annual report page:156).
- Add-backs and KPIs: Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, backlog, book-to-bill and free cash flow are in the releases (Q3 release page:10 to page:12) and backlog in the Q3 10-Q (page:27 to page:28).

- Debt and facility-level carrying values: Term Loan A, Term Loan B, senior notes and other debt in the Q3 10-Q debt table (page:10) with unamortised discount and financing costs shown as a total line only.

- Lease and pension terms: located in the annual report (Note 14 at page:151; Note 10 at page:139). Cash-paid interest and cash-paid income taxes: Not supplied. A search of all seven sources for interest paid, cash paid, taxes paid and supplemental cash flow information found only an accounting-standards sentence about future tax-paid disclosure; the cash flow statements printed (for example Q3 release page:8) show no such lines.
### Strongest contrary evidence and limitations

- Perimeter and comparability. The 10-K says the FY2025 statements include the merged business for the full year while FY2024 does not (page:118). Evidence: the statement of FY2024 perimeter. Risk mechanism: year-on-year growth for FY2025 over FY2024 is not like for like. Consequence: CP-1 must label that comparison and prefer the quarterly comparatives, which are both post-merger.

- Revenue base changes. The Q3 10-Q attributes lower revenue to contracts moving from consolidated to unconsolidated joint ventures and to fiscal year 2025 divestitures (page:23, page:25). Evidence: MD&A text. Risk mechanism: reported revenue and equity earnings are not comparable across periods. Consequence: the model should carry equity earnings and distributions separately.

- Management measures. Net leverage and Adjusted EBITDA are defined by management in the release (page:10). A figure computed by an analyst from statement lines will differ in definition. Consequence: both must be shown and labelled.

- Off-balance-sheet and contingent claims. Sales of receivables under the MARPA are disclosed (Q3 10-Q page:9); the debt note excludes them. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 should not read the debt table as the full financing claim without that note.
## Calculations

None performed. CP-0 does not normalise, reconcile or calculate figures. Coverage counts only: 168 pages (annual report), 24, 29 and 32 pages (quarterly reports), 12, 13 and 12 pages (releases), 290 pages in total, all retained; no page was excluded.

### Financial base view

The financial base is usable and the group is moderately levered but liquid. At July 3, 2026 principal debt was 3,875 against cash of 459 and undrawn revolver capacity of 917, and trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 1,128 gives gross leverage of 3.44x and net leverage of 3.03x, matching management's 3.0x. Leverage has fallen through FY2026 from 3.23x net at October 3, 2025, driven by a debt reduction of 133 (a voluntary 125 term loan B payment on June 30, 2026 and scheduled amortization) and a 24 rise in trailing Adjusted EBITDA. Trailing cash interest cover is 3.93x on interest paid of 287, an improvement from 3.61x for FY2025, alongside lower interest paid (175 against 194 in the nine months) and the April 2026 repricing (term loan B margin now 1.75% over Term SOFR, from 2.25%).

Three points qualify the picture. First, cash conversion is lower than margins suggest: nine-month operating cash flow of 235 was down on 273, free cash flow of 213 includes a net 120 inflow from selling receivables, and the group is guiding to an implied fourth-quarter free cash flow of 312 to 362 to reach its 525 to 575 range. Second, the earnings base includes equity earnings of 88 on a trailing basis (7.8% of trailing Adjusted EBITDA) and management add-backs of 76 in the nine months (Adjusted EBITDA 828 against company-defined EBITDA 752), so the headline measure is more generous than a plain operating measure; the financial maintenance covenant definition is not supplied. Third, the capital structure is mostly floating and secured: 2,866 of the 3,875 is term loan debt, hedged only by swaps with notional 1.3 billion that mature through January 31, 2027, and the senior notes (1,000 at 7.250%, due August 1, 2032) sit behind the secured facilities. Tangible equity is negative (equity of 4,789 against goodwill and intangibles of 7,378), so creditor protection rests on cash flows rather than hard assets. Revenue is shrinking (nine months 2026 down 2.5%) though margins and backlog (48.2 billion) are rising. Comparability limits: FY2025 had 53 weeks, and the FY2024 base excludes the merged business until September 27, 2024, so FY2024 ratios are not shown.

### Earnings quality and cash flow

Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income attributable to common shareholders adjusted for interest expense and other, net, income taxes, depreciation and amortization and discrete items: acquisition, transaction and integration costs, non-cash gains and losses, loss on extinguishment of debt, utilization of fair market value adjustments from purchase accounting, and stock-based compensation (10-K page:156; Q3 release page:9). Add-backs between company-defined EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA were 110 in FY2025 (85 of acquisition and integration costs, 12 of debt extinguishment, 21 of stock compensation, less 8 of fair market value utilization), 71 in 9M 2025 and 76 in 9M 2026 (36 of integration costs, 16 of debt extinguishment, 1 of fair market value utilization, 23 of stock compensation). Equity earnings of non-consolidated subsidiaries (73 in 9M 2026) are inside both EBITDA measures; distributions received were 87 in 9M 2026 against 57 in 9M 2025, so the cash returned exceeded the earnings recognized in the latest period.

Cash flow. 9M 2026 operating cash flow of 235 was 38 lower than 9M 2025; management attributes this to a 129 increase in cash earnings offset by 167 of working capital outflows (Q3 10-Q page:30). The nine-month outflows include a 160 reduction in accrued compensation and a 198 reduction in payables, contract liabilities and other current liabilities (Q3 10-Q page:4). Net cash from receivable sales was 120 in 9M 2026 against 42 in 9M 2025. Cash taxes were 26 against 67. Interest paid was 175 against 194. Investing cash flow was an outflow of 48 against an inflow of 236 in 9M 2025, which held the 358 of proceeds from the Rapid Solutions sale (Q3 release page:8). Financing outflow was 165 against 231.

Segments. Digital Solutions (DS) and Global Engineering Solutions (GES). Revenues and Adjusted EBITDA, in US$m: FY2025 DS 5,543 and 437, GES 8,850 and 667 (10-K page:157); 9M 2025 DS 4,047 and 321, GES 6,421 and 483; 9M 2026 DS 4,262 and 324, GES 5,943 and 504 (Q3 10-Q page:26 to page:27). Adjusted EBITDA margin on those figures: DS 7.9% FY2025, 7.9% 9M 2025, 7.6% 9M 2026; GES 7.5% FY2025, 7.5% 9M 2025, 8.5% 9M 2026. Management attributes lower GES revenue to contracts moving from consolidated to unconsolidated joint ventures, a fiscal 2025 divestiture, the government shutdown in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 and ramp-down of historical programs (Q3 10-Q page:23, page:25, page:27). Revenue by customer for 9M 2026: Department of War and U.S. Intelligence Community 5,334, other U.S. Government agencies 2,811, commercial and international 2,060 (Q3 10-Q page:7). Backlog was 48.2 billion at July 3, 2026, of which funded 6.2 billion; remaining performance obligations were 8.9 billion, with about 79% expected within 12 months (Q3 10-Q page:8, page:27).

- April 24, 2026 first amendment to the credit facility (disclosed as a subsequent event in the Q2 10-Q, page:17, and in the Q3 10-Q debt note, page:11): new term loan A of 1,400 due April 24, 2031; existing term loan reduced and amended into a new term loan B of 1,591 due September 27, 2031 at a lower margin; revolver increased by 150 to 1,000 with maturity extended to April 24, 2031; letter of credit subfacility raised to 250 and swingline to 150. Cash flow shows borrowing proceeds of 2,991 and repayments of 3,106 in Q3 2026 (Q3 release page:8).

### Business and transaction view

Amentum is a global advanced engineering and technology solutions provider to U.S. and allied governments, organised in two segments (Digital Solutions and Global Engineering Solutions). It exists in its present form since September 27, 2024, when the Jacobs Critical Mission Solutions business and parts of the Jacobs Divergent Solutions business were spun off and merged with the legacy Amentum business in a Reverse Morris Trust. Creditors therefore lend to a company that has existed as a combined entity for about two years, that carries purchase-accounting intangibles and goodwill (7,378 of 11,199 of total assets at July 3, 2026), and whose pre-merger history does not include the larger business.

The operating model is low-capital and contract-based. Roughly four-fifths of revenue is from the U.S. Government, mostly as prime contractor, with about 56% of 9M 2026 revenue on cost-plus-fee contracts that pass through inflation and a rising fixed-price share. Visibility is large in headline terms (backlog 48.2 billion) but only 6.2 billion is funded, so revenue durability depends on appropriations and option exercise rather than signed funding. The principal operating risks the filings describe are budget timing (shutdowns from October 2, 2025 to November 12, 2025 and a partial shutdown from January 31, 2026 to February 3, 2026), contract compliance and audit exposure, joint venture structure changes that reduce consolidated revenue while moving profit into equity earnings, and estimate catch-ups on fixed-price work.

Financial policy so far is creditor-friendly: no dividends, no share repurchases in FY2025, debt prepayments from divestiture proceeds and cash, and a stated priority of reducing debt. The weaknesses for a creditor are in control and documentation rather than behaviour: the sponsor-linked stockholder keeps board nomination rights tied to its ownership, the tax-free merger structure restricts some strategic actions, and the credit agreement, its April 2026 amendment, the indenture and the tax matters agreement are not supplied, so capacity to pay out cash, incur debt or release collateral cannot be tested. Evidence on creditor-adverse behaviour (priming, uptiering, drop-downs) is neither found nor testable.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The defining transaction closed on September 27, 2024. Legacy Amentum (Amentum Parent Holdings LLC, owned by Amentum Joint Venture LP) merged with the spin-off of the Jacobs Critical Mission Solutions business and portions of the Jacobs Divergent Solutions business in a tax-efficient Reverse Morris Trust. Amentum Parent Holdings LLC was the accounting acquirer and is the predecessor, so statements before September 27, 2024 exclude the acquired business and are not comparable (10-K page:117, page:128). Before the spin-off the acquired business reorganised under a new company, distributed a cash payment of about 911 million to Jacobs, and Jacobs distributed about 80.95% of its shares to Jacobs shareholders (10-K page:6 to page:7, page:128). Immediately after closing there were about 243 million shares outstanding, held 58.5% by Jacobs and its shareholders and 37.0% by Amentum Joint Venture LP, with 4.5% placed in escrow; in March 2025 the escrow was released, 3.5% to the former Jacobs holders and 1.0% to the sponsor stockholder (10-K page:128). Consideration transferred was 3,948 and total consideration 4,032 including a previously held joint venture interest, and goodwill was recognised at 3,004 on final allocation (10-K page:129 to page:131). Status: completed, with purchase accounting finalised in FY2025.

New debt at the Transaction: a seven-year term facility of 3,750 and a five-year revolver of 850 under a credit agreement dated September 27, 2024 with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent, plus 1,000 of 7.250% senior notes due August 1, 2032 issued August 13, 2024 into escrow and released at closing. Proceeds of the credit facility were used together with other cash sources to repay in full the prior first lien and second lien credit agreements and to pay related fees and expenses (10-K page:145, page:149). The filing does not state a sources-and-uses split, so how much of the borrowing funded the 911 payment to Jacobs is Not supplied. An equity contribution of 235 from the legacy equityholder immediately before the Transaction is disclosed (10-K page:153).

Later debt events. In FY2025 the company made voluntary term loan payments of about 191 (June 27, 2025), 250 (July 31, 2025) and 281 (September 30, 2025), together 722, after selling the Rapid Solutions hardware and product business, part of Digital Solutions, to Lockheed Martin Corporation on June 26, 2025 for 360 in cash (10-K page:98, page:105, page:132, page:145). On April 24, 2026 a first amendment to the credit facility (executed; the amendment itself is not in the pack) created a 1,400 term loan A due April 24, 2031, amended the existing term loan into a 1,591 term loan B due September 27, 2031 on lower margins, and raised the revolver by 150 to 1,000 with maturity April 24, 2031 (Q2 10-Q page:17; Q3 10-Q page:11 to page:12). The business strategy states reliance in part on acquisitions and strategic investments to sustain growth, as well as targeted divestitures (10-K page:23 risk factor list); one acquisition-related cash outflow (70, the working capital settlement for the Transaction) and one divestiture occurred in FY2025 (10-K page:116, page:130), and 9M 2026 shows no acquisition spend (Q3 10-Q page:4). No acquisition appetite is inferred from these. Contributions to equity method investments were 53 in 9M 2026 against 36 in 9M 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:4), a use of cash that supports the joint venture strategy. 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: 81% of revenue from direct U.S. Government contracts, backlog of 48.2 billion with 6.2 billion funded (10-K page:8; Q3 10-Q page:27). Credit implication: debt service risk comes from timing and liquidity, not demand collapse; a liquidity cushion of 1,376 at July 3, 2026 (financial handoff) is the relevant mitigant. Counter: the rating-statement conflict does not affect this.

2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: fixed-price share rose to 29% of 9M 2026 revenue from 24% in FY2025, and net favorable estimate adjustments of 83 against 40 (Q3 10-Q page:8, page:27). Risk mechanic: fixed-price work carries cost overrun risk and catch-up adjustments move reported profit between periods. Credit implication: Adjusted EBITDA of 1,128 on a trailing basis may include non-recurring catch-up benefit; leverage of 3.44x gross and 3.03x net is more sensitive to margin slippage than the headline suggests. Counter: cost-plus work remains 56% of revenue.

3. Concentration. Evidence: Department of War and Intelligence Community 5,334 of 10,205 in 9M 2026, and the U.S. Government at 80% in total (Q3 10-Q page:7). Risk mechanic: shifts in defense or intelligence budgets, contract recompetes, or protests concentrate effects. Credit implication: single-sovereign dependence limits diversification; debarment or a large program loss is a tail risk with the greatest effect on enterprise value and on a collateral package secured by substantially all assets.

4. Sponsor alignment and creditor control. Evidence: no dividends and repurchases, voluntary prepayments, board nomination rights linked to ownership, tax-free merger restrictions (10-K page:24, page:71, page:93). Risk mechanic: a holder with board influence could favour distributions or recapitalisations when leverage falls; the restricted-payment capacity in the credit agreement is not visible. Credit implication: current behaviour supports deleveraging, but the sources do not allow a view on whether the documents would stop a distribution; monitoring should track holder changes and the amended credit agreement.

5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: no credit agreement, amendment, indenture or tax matters agreement in the pack; no ratings report; current holdings unknown. Risk mechanic: covenant, priming and payout analysis cannot be performed. Credit implication: conclusions on creditor control are provisional.

1. Government share of FY2025 revenue = (7,678 + 3,994) / 14,393 = 11,672 / 14,393 = 81.1%, against the stated 81% (10-K page:8, page:133).
2. Government share of 9M 2026 revenue = (5,334 + 2,811) / 10,205 = 8,145 / 10,205 = 79.8%, shown as 80%. Department of War and Intelligence Community share = 5,334 / 10,205 = 52.3%.

4. Funded backlog share = 6,240 / 48,237 = 12.9% (Q3 10-Q page:28). Unfunded = 41,997, shown as 42.0 billion.
5. Prime share = 9,291 / 10,205 = 91.0% (Q3 10-Q page:8). International revenue change = 2,204 / 2,711 - 1 = -18.7%.

6. Estimate adjustments: increase in net favorable adjustments = 83 - 40 = 43; increase in nine-month Adjusted EBITDA = 828 - 804 = 24. Net favorable adjustments as a share of 9M 2026 Adjusted EBITDA = 83 / 828 = 10.0%. This comparison is an analyst reading: the adjustments are recognised in revenue, and the filing does not give their EBITDA effect, so the equivalence is assumed (an EPS effect of 0.27 against 0.13 is printed).
7. Equity earnings share of 9M 2026 Adjusted EBITDA = 73 / 828 = 8.8%. Capital spending share of revenue = 22 / 10,205 = 0.2%.

8. Ownership at the Transaction: 58.5% and 37.0% with 4.5% escrowed; after release, 58.5% + 3.5% = 62.0% for former Jacobs holders and 37.0% + 1.0% = 38.0% for the equityholder side. This is the issue-date allocation only; later transfers are Not supplied.

9. Voluntary term loan payments in FY2025 = 191 + 250 + 281 = 722, equal to the 722 stated (10-K page:98). Divestiture proceeds: purchase price 360, net cash conveyed 365 in the cash flow statement (10-K page:116); the 5 difference is not explained in the sources read.

spans.text: ## Request

This synthesis covers Amentum Holdings, Inc. (the consolidated group) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit_snapshot pathway. It draws only on the source-readiness, financial and business handoffs, which cover FY2025 and the quarter ended July 3, 2026, and adds no outside information. It gives a fundamental credit view without peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
### Issuer sources behind the upstream handoffs
This module reads no source text. The figures and facts come from the upstream handoffs, which relied on these pinned sources.

### Context and handoffs
- Run context (settings, not issuer evidence): sha256 f35913dfc940216c52100a4ebad511585e07d7ab0e645bded7b78046135f5c43.
- Supplied handoff: CP-0 (source readiness), sha256 a73cd36f054f9d1f45a1a722b687f0bbcf428fae01c4dbd0e0acf28f5952073e.
- Supplied handoff: CP-1 (financial base), sha256 3f7716d0288dc98301a065f43c1a1aafb7f2ca57911372ef5ca1732285e0a677. Basis for every figure below, quoted unchanged.
- Supplied handoff: CP-1A (business and transaction context), sha256 d5fb957740351fe382b18b816f2170cd01ce1de250ef7cfa5c0a7e961eb95b91. Basis for every business fact below.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Amentum Holdings, Inc. has sound liquidity of USD 1,376 million and net leverage of 3.03x, down from 3.23x, supported by U.S. Government revenue; thin cash conversion and untested loan terms limit the view. | Medium | The credit agreement, its April 2026 amendment, ratings and current ownership are not in the sources, so covenant and creditor-control conclusions are provisional. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Liquidity is USD 1,376 million (cash USD 459 million, undrawn revolver USD 917 million), and the revolver matures April 24, 2031. | No committed facility expires within twelve months, and near-term debt service is well covered. | High |

| Net leverage is 3.03x at July 3, 2026 against 3.23x at FY2025, and cash interest cover is 3.93x against 3.61x. | Debt service capacity is improving, but leverage remains above 3x and depends on a management EBITDA measure. | Medium |

| Nine-month free cash flow was USD 213 million, or USD 93 million without a USD 120 million receivable-sales inflow. | Cash conversion is weaker than margins suggest, and the guidance implies a fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 312 million to USD 362 million. | Medium |
| About 74% of debt is floating rate, and swaps of USD 1.3 billion mature by January 31, 2027. | Interest cost becomes more exposed to rates after the hedges expire. | Medium |

| Funded backlog is USD 6.2 billion of USD 48.2 billion, and goodwill and intangibles are 7,378 of 11,199 of total assets. | Revenue visibility is conditional on appropriations, and creditor protection rests on cash flows rather than hard assets. | Medium |
### Credit view

Amentum Holdings, Inc. has an adequate and improving credit profile with sound liquidity, but its leverage, thin cash conversion and untested loan documents leave limited room for error. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,376 million, net leverage of 3.03x (3.23x at FY2025) and cash interest cover of 3.93x, backed by revenue that is 81% U.S. Government and a backlog of USD 48.2 billion. The weakest point is cash generation: nine-month free cash flow of USD 213 million falls to USD 93 million without a USD 120 million receivable-sales inflow, and guidance implies fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 312 million to USD 362 million. The outcome turns on whether that cash arrives, on the expiry of USD 1.3 billion of interest rate swaps by January 31, 2027, and on credit agreement terms the sources do not supply.
### Assessment and thesis

Fundamental credit view (Analyst Interpretation, confidence Medium). Basis: financial handoff (leverage, cover, liquidity, cash flow tables) and business handoff (customer, backlog, contract mix, financial policy rows). Business risk is moderate: the customer is largely the U.S. Government, which removes customer credit loss but exposes revenue timing to appropriations, and the contract mix is moving toward fixed price. Financial risk is moderate: net leverage of 3.03x and gross leverage of 3.44x on trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,128 million, a floating-rate structure, and cash conversion that depends on receivable sales and on catch-up adjustments. Liquidity is a strength. Confidence is Medium rather than High because the credit agreement, the first amendment, the indenture, ratings and current ownership are not supplied, and because the business handoff judged this synthesis as ready with limitations.

Thesis (Analyst Interpretation): Amentum Holdings, Inc. is a de-levering, liquid government contractor whose debt service rests on timely federal funding and on cash conversion that has yet to match its reported earnings, with creditor protections that the available evidence does not allow us to test.
### Key findings

First, liquidity and refinancing risk are low in the near term. The group holds cash of USD 459 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 917 million, a total of USD 1,376 million (Documentary Fact; financial handoff liquidity table). The April 24, 2026 amendment moved the revolver and the new term loan A out to April 24, 2031 and repriced term loan B (Documentary Fact; business handoff, new debt events). Scheduled principal over the next twelve months is about USD 50.9 million on the indicative schedule, small against liquidity. The indicative profile is back-ended: about 92% of scheduled principal falls in the years ending September 2031 and 2032, which defers refinancing risk but concentrates it.

Second, leverage is moderate and falling, but its quality depends on a management measure. Net leverage was 3.03x and gross leverage 3.44x at July 3, 2026, against 3.23x and 3.63x at FY2025 (Documentary Fact; financial handoff leverage table). On EBITDA before management adjustments, net leverage is 3.37x (financial handoff). Add-backs of USD 76 million in the nine months and equity earnings equal to 7.8% of trailing Adjusted EBITDA sit inside the denominator, and the trailing period spans 53 weeks (financial handoff gaps). The improvement from 3.23x is therefore real but flatters slightly.

Third, cash conversion lags reported earnings. Nine-month operating cash flow was USD 235 million against USD 273 million a year earlier, and free cash flow of USD 213 million includes a net USD 120 million inflow from selling receivables (Documentary Fact; financial handoff). The guidance ranges imply fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 312 million to USD 362 million against USD 261 million in the prior-year fourth quarter, which had 14 weeks (financial handoff calculation 14; Management Language for the guidance itself). The fourth quarter is therefore the test of whether conversion improves.

Fourth, business risk is anchored by the customer but not by funding. About 81% of FY2025 revenue came from direct U.S. Government contracts and backlog is USD 48.2 billion, but funded backlog is USD 6.2 billion (Documentary Fact; business handoff, customers and visibility rows). Shutdowns in the first half of FY2026 delayed awards and reduced revenue. Revenue fell 2.5% in the nine months and management lowered its FY2026 revenue range while raising the low end of its Adjusted EBITDA range, so margin gains, partly from favorable contract estimate adjustments of USD 83 million against USD 40 million, are carrying earnings (Analyst Interpretation; business handoff, estimate catch-ups row).

Fifth, creditor-control conclusions cannot be drawn. The credit agreement, its amendment, the indenture and the tax matters agreement are not supplied, the amended covenant level is unknown (the only printed level is the pre-amendment 5.00x first lien net leverage maximum, against an indicative 2.13x), and current holdings of the sponsor-linked stockholder, who holds board nomination rights, are not disclosed (Insufficient Information).
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Liquidity (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): USD 1,376 million of liquidity with no drawings on the revolver and the first committed maturity in April 2031. Deleveraging record (Documentary Fact; financial and business handoffs): total debt fell from USD 4,008 million to USD 3,875 million, net leverage from 3.23x to 3.03x, with voluntary term loan payments of USD 722 million in FY2025 and USD 125 million in June 2026 and no dividends or buybacks. Customer quality and visibility (Documentary Fact; business handoff): 81% of FY2025 revenue from U.S. Government contracts, 91% prime contractor revenue in the nine months, backlog of USD 48.2 billion and remaining performance obligations of USD 8.9 billion, of which about 79% fall within twelve months. Asset-light, cost-plus-weighted model (Documentary Fact; both handoffs): 56% of nine-month revenue on cost-plus contracts, which limits inflation risk, and capital spending of USD 22 million in the nine months, about 0.2% of revenue. Lower interest burden (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): cash interest cover of 3.93x against 3.61x, helped by the April 2026 repricing of term loan B to a 1.75% margin.

Weaknesses. Cash conversion (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; financial handoff): free cash flow of USD 93 million in the nine months excluding receivable sales, against a reported USD 213 million; the programme has a maximum of USD 400 million and USD 300 million was sold and outstanding. Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation; both handoffs): Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,128 million against USD 1,013 million before adjustments; equity earnings inside the measure; a 53-week trailing period; and a rise of USD 43 million in net favorable estimate adjustments that exceeds the USD 24 million rise in nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, which suggests underlying earnings growth was smaller, although the filing does not give the EBITDA effect. Interest-rate exposure (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): about 74% of debt is floating rate, hedged by swaps of USD 1.3 billion that mature through January 31, 2027, and the company puts the nine-month sensitivity at about USD 23 million per one percentage point. Balance sheet composition (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): goodwill and intangibles of USD 7,378 million are 66% of total assets, so tangible equity is negative USD 2,589 million, and creditor value rests on contract cash flows. Revenue and funding conditionality (Documentary Fact; business handoff): funded backlog is 12.9% of total backlog, revenue declined 2.5% in the nine months, and fixed-price work rose to 29% of revenue from 24%. Documentation and control (Insufficient Information; business handoff): no loan documents, ratings or current ownership, so payout capacity, collateral release and covenant headroom cannot be tested; the tax-free merger structure also limits some strategic actions.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Cash conversion shortfall | Operating cash flow depends on working capital, receivable sales (net inflow USD 120 million in the nine months) and a required fourth-quarter step-up | Free cash flow available for debt reduction may fall short of guidance, slowing deleveraging from 3.03x | Material | Financial handoff cash flow tables, calculation 14 |

| Interest rate and hedge roll-off | About 74% of debt is floating rate and swaps of USD 1.3 billion end by January 31, 2027 | Higher interest cost reduces cash interest cover from 3.93x | Material | Financial handoff debt table |

| Federal funding and concentration | 80% of nine-month revenue is U.S. Government; funded backlog is USD 6.2 billion; shutdowns and continuing resolutions delay awards and billing | Revenue and cash timing volatility; liquidity of USD 1,376 million is the buffer | Material | Business handoff customer and visibility rows |

| Earnings quality | Catch-up adjustments, add-backs, equity earnings and a 53-week trailing period raise reported Adjusted EBITDA | Reported leverage of 3.03x may understate leverage on a cleaner basis | Material | Financial handoff definition review; business handoff estimate row |

| Back-ended maturities | About 92% of indicative scheduled principal falls in the years ending September 2031 and 2032 | Refinancing risk is concentrated in two years and depends on market access and leverage then | Material | Financial handoff maturity table (indicative) |

| Asset coverage | Goodwill and intangibles are 66% of total assets; collateral is substantially all assets of an asset-light business | Loss given default would depend on enterprise value from contract cash flows rather than tangible assets | Material | Financial handoff balance sheet rows |

| Compliance and debarment | Government audits and investigations could lead to repayments, fines or suspension or debarment; none is currently expected to be material | Low probability but severe effect on a business this dependent on federal contracts | Minor | Business handoff compliance row |

| Control and documentation | Sponsor-linked board nomination rights, tax-free merger restrictions and unsupplied loan documents | Payout, debt incurrence and collateral capacity cannot be tested; evidence is insufficient, not adverse | Minor | Business handoff governance rows |

No new calculation. Every figure is taken unchanged from the financial handoff (leverage, cover, liquidity, cash flow, maturity and balance sheet tables and calculations 1 to 15) or the business handoff (customer, backlog, contract mix and estimate rows). Cross-checks repeated here: net leverage 3,416 / 1,128 = 3.03x; liquidity 459 + 917 = 1,376; free cash flow excluding receivable sales 213 - 120 = 93; goodwill and intangibles share 7,378 / 11,199 = 66%.
